title: Ben Martin's Riviera band, Camarata and first lessons
summary: Camarata gets him into Barnet's band; Billie Fisher and a rigid teacher begin his study; Camarata learns to write from Joe Moore.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: We also played with that band Ben Martin's Riviera at the Jersey shore. In that band was Tootie Camarata, who became, I guess, a famous pops conductor later on. And Chris Griffin who was a trumpet player at CBS for many, many years; Joe Moody. He wasn't directly involved in that one but it all came about from getting to know Joe in that period; he had his own group.

Tootie got a job with Charlie Barnet and got me in there and at that point I left Columbia. I had begun to take lessons-- the first lessons were with Archie Bleyer, and there was a guy named Billie Fisher--there was a Scott Fisher too at that time--I don't know if it does anything to you. They had a band, a North Jersey band, Billie was a precocious sort of saxophone player and arranger. He became an arranger for CBS for many, many years; he had gotten very commercial. I'm trying to remember the connection.

this, Tootie got involved and Tootie was interested in writing, as I was. Tootie used to take down dictation from Joe Moore/ who was blind. Joe on the piano would tell him what notes to put where and who to give it to. He'd hear all this and Tootie learned to write this way.

At one point we decided we were going to take some lessons and we both went to an old style--I wouldn't call him a martinette, but a very rigid instrucoor type that Billie Fisher had and his name was (inaudible). That began the whole thing of studying. Tootie did it too.

Later on we both went to Teacher's College. At that point Tootie went off with Jimmy Dorsey and started to make a big name for himself. I stuck there, I went with Benny but I didn't make a big name for myself. That was after and we're jumping the gun here.
